title: Troubleshooting AI Red Teaming Broker Issues

blocks.text: The AI Security Red Teaming Broker is a lightweight agent that you deploy inside your network to enable Red Teaming to reach private AI applications without opening inbound firewall ports. Use this article to diagnose and resolve common broker connectivity, authentication, and routing issues.

For any broker issue, your first step is always to run the built-in diagnostic tool airt-broker diagnose. It checks connectivity, certificates, OAuth credentials, and DNS without disrupting a live broker.

blocks.text: This section describes common Broker issues and the steps to resolve them:

blocks.item: Broker Stays Pending or Offline
Symptom: The broker status does not change from Pending, or it repeatedly switches to Offline. The logs show repeated opening wss entries with no wss connected line.
The following are the likely causes:
Cannot Reach the Gateway
Confirm that outbound TCP access to the GATEWAY_URL host on port 443 is open.
Run the preflight check and review the DNS, TCP, and TLS rows.
Invalid OAuth Credentials (diagnose shows 401 invalid_client)
Go to Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers and open the broker's detail page.
Compare the OAUTH_CLIENT_ID and OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET values in your deployment against the Authentication Service credentials associated with this broker registration.
If they do not match, re-copy the credentials from the Authentication Service API client and redeploy the broker container.
Egress IP Not in the Allow-List (4403 gateway_cidr_rejected)
Identify the broker container's public egress IP address.
Go to Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers and open the broker's detail page.
Under Source-IP Allow-list, add the broker's public egress IP.
Allow-list changes apply immediately and no broker restart is required.
Broker ID Mismatch or Broker is Revoked (4401 gateway_broker_unregistered or _revoked)
Confirm that the BROKER_ID environment variable in your deployment matches the ID shown on the broker's detail page in AIRT.
If the broker status shows Revoked, go to Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers, open the broker, and select Reinstate.
TLS Certificate Errors
Symptom: Broker startup logs show certificate verify failed or unable to get local issuer certificate.
Cause: A corporate TLS inspection proxy or a private Certificate Authority (CA) is intercepting the broker's outbound connection.
To resolve this issue:
Obtain the corporate CA certificate in PEM format.
Set the EXTRA_CA_CERTS environment variable to the path of the PEM file and mount it into the container:
-e EXTRA_CA_CERTS="/etc/airt-broker/corp-intermediates.pem" \ -v "$PWD/certs:/etc/airt-broker:ro"
If an outbound proxy is required, also set:
-e HTTPS_PROXY="http://proxy.internal:8080"
Do not set SSL_VERIFY to false. Disabling certificate validation removes a critical security control and is not supported in production environments.
Broker is Online but Tests Return 403
Symptom: The broker shows Online in AIRT, but test requests return a 403 error.
Cause: The target's base URL is not in the broker's target allow-list.
To resolve this issue:
Go to Administration > Red Teaming > Brokers and open the broker's detail page.
Select the Allow-lists tab, then select Target URLs.
Add the target's base URL, or verify that the X-Target-Url header in your request is correct.
Tests Time Out (504) or Fail with 502
Symptom: Requests hang and return 504 Gateway Timeout or 502 Bad Gateway.
Cause: The target application is slow to respond or is unreachable from the broker host.
To resolve this issue:
From the broker host, verify that the broker can reach the target URL directly (for example, using curl <target-url>).
If the target is reachable but responds slowly, increase the request timeout:
-e TARGET_REQUEST_TIMEOUT=120
Check that no firewall rule is blocking traffic from the broker host to the target application.
Broker Disconnects Periodically While Idle
Symptom: Logs show wss disconnected with close_code: null and abnormal: true after a period of inactivity, followed by automatic reconnection (opening wss).
Cause: An intermediary (proxy, NAT gateway, or firewall) is closing idle connections due to a configured timeout.

This behavior is benign. The broker reconnects automatically. If reconnections are frequent and affecting test reliability, work with your network team to increase the idle connection timeout on the intermediary.

blocks.text: If you cannot resolve the issue, collect the following information before contacting Zscaler Support:
Run these commands to export a redacted diagnostic report and recent broker logs:
docker exec <broker-container> python -m airt_broker diagnose --json > diag.json docker logs --tail 500 <broker-container> > broker.log
Ensure you include the following information when you contact support:

blocks.item: diag.json
broker.log
Your BROKER_ID
The approximate date and time of the incident
The diag.json output is automatically redacted and does not contain your OAUTH_CLIENT_SECRET. Do not share your client secret directly with support or include it in log files.
